## Findings
- claim-1: **Theorem.** Let \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) be bigrassmannian, with \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Put \[ q=n-r,\quad i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j), \] \[ A=\Lambda/I_{r,q},\qquad Q=J_v/A_+J_v. \] Then both \[ G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\} \quad\text{and}\quad G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\} \] map to homogeneous integral bases of \(Q\). Hence both families minimally generate \(J_v\). In particular, \[ Q\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z\,e_\rho,\qquad \deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|, \] \[ H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z, \] and \(Q_d\) is torsion-free. The basis \(e_\rho\) admits the perfect integral degree-complement pairing \[ \langle e_\rho,e_\sigma\rangle=\delta_{\sigma,\rho^\vee},\qquad \rho^\vee=(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1), \] between \(Q_d\) and \(Q_{2ij+ab-d}\). The lower-family generation and its no-syzygy mechanism are grounded in the supplied full text. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- claim-2: A parameter-uniform closed formula for the unimodular change-of-basis matrix from the ordered \(G_L\)-basis to the ordered \(G_R\)-basis is not established.
## Strategy

**Hypotheses.** Let \(\Lambda\) be the integral symmetric-function ring, \(q=n-r\), \(I_{r,q}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\}\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), and \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\). For a bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\), let \(J_v\) be its Grassmannian basic ideal in \(A\), and put
\[
i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad
a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j),\quad Q=J_v/A_+J_v.
\]
Then
\[
G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\},\qquad
G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}.
\]

**Dependency boundary.** The audited proof uses accepted attempts `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1` (integral lower-family kernel certificate), `-301-1` (integral graded quotient conjugation), `-286-1` (right-family transfer), `-264-1` (quotient invariance under conjugation), and `-317-1` (Gaussian enumerator and complement pairing). The lower-family generation/minimality theorem is grounded at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]; the no-syzygy result used in the kernel argument is at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-825]. No finite computation is used.

**Consolidated proof.** Let \(F_L\) be the graded free abelian group on \(G_L\), with the generator indexed by \(\rho\) in degree \(ij+|\rho|\). Accepted generation gives \(F_L\twoheadrightarrow Q\). By `-296-1`, a nonzero homogeneous kernel element reduces integrally to a nonzero homogeneous source-form syzygy among the \(\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}\); the source no-syzygy theorem excludes this. Hence
\[
F_L\xrightarrow{\sim}Q,
\qquad
Q=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z e_\rho,
\quad \deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|.
\]
This includes \(a=0\).

By `-301-1` and `-264-1`, partition conjugation is an integral graded isomorphism on the relevant quotients and carries \(A_+J_v\) to the conjugate positive-degree product. By `-286-1`, it carries the lower basis for the conjugate parameters to \(G_R\). Thus \(G_R\) also maps to a homogeneous integral basis of \(Q\). Since both families generate \(J_v\), basis independence in \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\) makes each family irredundant, hence minimal.

Finally, `-317-1` counts \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) and supplies the complement involution
\[
\rho^\vee=(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1).
\]
Therefore
\[
H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z,
\]
each \(Q_d\) is torsion-free, and
\[
\langle e_\rho,e_\sigma\rangle=\delta_{\sigma,\rho^\vee}
\]
is a perfect integral pairing \(Q_d\times Q_{2ij+ab-d}\to\mathbb Z\).

**Verdict.** The requested target is established: both \(G_L\) and \(G_R\) are homogeneous integral bases of \(Q\) and minimally generate \(J_v\), with the stated Hilbert series, torsion-freeness, and pairing.

## Gaps

- **Optional statement, [unsupported].** No parameter-uniform closed formula for the ordered unimodular transition matrix from \(G_L\) to \(G_R\) is established.
